_readme: The one golden threshold file. Every number below was hard-coded in exactly one
consumer before ST-09; the same number now lives here once and each consumer is
checked against it by a drift test (Go: control-plane/internal/session/
This file is the SPEC, the code is the copy. Changing a number here without
changing the consumer fails the drift test, which is the point: a threshold that
moves silently is how five vocabularies of 'is this healthy' drifted apart.
`version` is what a Verdict reports as `thresholds_version`. Bump it whenever any
value changes, so a stored verdict can be read against the thresholds it was

classifier.hitch_sd_ms.why: Present-interval sigma at or above this is a hitch. AS-04: clean paths sit at 2-10 ms and the 0.5% loss condition drove sigma to 27-32 ms, so 18 sits above clean and below loss.

classifier.encoder_ceiling_ms.why: One frame at 60 fps is 16.7 ms; an encode p95 at or above 16 ms means the encoder has no headroom left at the reference frame rate.

classifier.congestion_loss_delta.why: Packets lost across the window must climb by more than a handful before loss is called congestion rather than noise.

classifier.congestion_rtt_p95_ms.why: Loss alone can be a lossy-but-short link; congestion is loss AND a queue, and a p95 RTT over 50 ms on the paths this serves means a queue.

classifier.min_host_fps.why: p10 of host encoder fps at or above this is 'steady'. Below it the host is the suspect, so the client-presentation and nominal verdicts both refuse to fire.

classifier.hitch_min_samples.why: How many present-interval sigma samples must reach hitch_sd_ms before the window is a hitch. The rule used to be a MAX: on 2026-08-23 a healthy 300 s session flipped to likely_client_presentation_limit on ONE sample of 18.058 out of 54. Two is the smallest number that makes the claim about the window rather than about one sample.

classifier.warmup_exclude_s.why: Seconds after a session reaches RUNNING whose samples are excluded from hitch detection and the encoder.fps floor. The first seconds judder and under-run by construction (pipeline filling, receiver buffer inflating, encoder ramping); inside a 300 s window they otherwise sit as permanent unsatisfied falsifiers for the rest of the session. Reported as window.warmup_excluded_ms so the exclusion is visible.

agent.encoder_stall_ms.why: Encoder OUTPUT silence at or above this, while INPUT keeps arriving, is a stall. One second is ~60 frames at 60 fps and ~17x the drop-timeout's per-frame reasoning (500 ms, which asks 'did THIS frame produce output') — this asks 'has the encoder stopped'. Before candidate 8 there was no encoder.stall event, metric or counter at all: interpipe_queue_level_max was the nearest signal, and a 2026-08-22 investigation read a peer-rejected HEVC m-line as a ring stall for hours.

health.network_degrading_after_s.why: How long ABR must sit at or below the profile floor before the session's health state says the network is degrading, rather than reacting to one bad window.

health.abr_at_floor_after_s.why: Sustained at the floor: quality cannot drop further within this profile, so say so rather than keep promising improvement.

health.unsustainable_after_s.why: Three minutes pinned at the floor is a profile the network cannot carry; this is the only health threshold that fails a session.

client_health.degrade_sustain_s.why: A client-reported degradation must persist this long before it moves the session's health state — one bad 1 s sample is not a device verdict.

client_health.smooth_sustain_s.why: Recovery is slower to believe than degradation (30 s vs 20 s): clearing back to healthy on a brief calm patch would flap the banner.

web.client_health.present_sd_degraded_ms.why: Deliberately well over the AS-05 controller's DEGRADED_SD_MS (18): the playout controller reacts at 18, the CLIENT HEALTH class only blames the device once the buffer's own remedy has demonstrably failed.

web.client_health.present_p95_degraded_m.why: A sustained long-frame tail; sigma can stay modest while p95 shows repeated doubled frames.

web.client_health.freeze_degraded_count.why: One freeze in a window is a blip; two is a pattern.

web.client_health.decode_budget_fraction.why: Decode time at 85% of the per-frame budget leaves no room for compositing and present, so the device is already the limit even though frames still land.

web.client_health.decode_abs_ceiling_ms.why: Fallback ceiling when the profile frame budget is unknown (0).

web.present_cadence.min_samples.why: Fewer intervals than this in a 1 s window is not a cadence, it is a fragment (a hidden tab, or a window the RVFC loop barely filled). Every present_* summary is null below it rather than confidently wrong. Web-only consumer.

web.present_cadence.doubled_band.why: An interval counts as 'doubled' when it lands within +/-20% of exactly 2x the median. Wide enough to catch a missed vsync under normal scheduling noise, narrow enough that a 2.5x stall falls outside it and is counted as a long frame instead. Web-only consumer.

web.present_cadence.long_frame_factor.why: An interval longer than 2.5x the median is not the vsync beat: it sits above the top of the doubled band, so it is a genuine stall and must never be excused as inherent. Web-only consumer.

web.present_cadence.beat_doubled_max.why: At source fps == display Hz a beat of up to a quarter of the window is the expected consequence of two free-running clocks (the 2026-08-22 1440p120 session sat near 12%). Above this the pattern is too dense to be the beat, so inherentBeat refuses to fire and the reader is not told the window is fine. Web-only consumer.

web.playout.default_ms.why: #108: the measured smoothness knee — present sigma plateaus at a buttery 2-3 ms from ~100 ms of receiver buffer onward.

web.playout.floor_ms.why: T2 (2026-08-18) playout knee: 50 ms buys 4.7x fewer client-present drops than 30 ms for +24 ms glass-to-glass, and removes a bimodal 9% drop failure mode.

web.playout.cap_ms.why: Hard ceiling on the buffer (AS-00 Component 4) — past this the latency cost exceeds any smoothness left to buy.

web.playout.step_down_ms.why: Conservative descent per healthy 5 s window, before a healthy streak earns the faster step.

web.playout.step_up_factor.why: Fast up / gated down: a single degraded window multiplies the buffer, because re-inflating late costs a visible hitch and re-inflating early costs milliseconds.

web.playout.hold_ms.why: Default dwell after any step-up before descending again — slower than ABR's retarget cadence, so this loop never chases an ABR transient.

web.playout.hold_fast_ms.why: IL-1: shortened dwell once the path is confirmed locally healthy, so a clean LAN reaches the floor in seconds.

web.playout.step_down_fast_ms.why: IL-1 accelerated descent step, paired with hold_fast_ms.

web.playout.healthy_sd_ms.why: AS-04 used sigma < 12 ms as the healthy line everywhere; at or below this the controller may trim the buffer.

web.playout.degraded_sd_ms.why: At or above this the controller re-inflates. The 12-18 ms hysteresis band holds (no change), so the loop cannot chatter around one threshold.

web.playout.healthy_streak_for_fast.why: Three consecutive healthy 5 s evaluations = 15 s of confirmed local health before fast descent is trusted; long enough to ride out an ABR retarget wiggle.

web.playout.eval_interval_ms.why: The design's 5 s evaluation window (AS-00 Component 4).

web.signal.sd_poor_ms.why: Connection glyph: AS-04 'degraded'. Same number as web.playout.degraded_sd_ms on purpose — the glyph must not disagree with the controller acting on the same sigma.

web.signal.sd_fair_ms.why: Connection glyph: AS-04 'watch'. Same number as web.playout.healthy_sd_ms.

web.signal.sd_excellent_ms.why: Below this and clean, the stream is at the #108 knee — the only reading that earns four bars.

web.signal.packets_lost_poor.why: Packets lost in one 1 s poll window at or above this is heavy loss regardless of how smooth presentation still looks.

web.signal.packets_lost_fair.why: Some loss — enough to knock the glyph down one rung, not enough to call the connection poor.

web.clock.repost_interval_s.why: How often the client re-posts its clock-offset estimate while connected. The offset was posted ONCE per session and latched, so a drifting clock silently invalidated every aligned series for the rest of the session while bench mode read a different, live estimate. One minute is far slower than any measurement cost and far faster than observed drift.

web.clock.repost_delta_ms.why: Only re-post when the new estimate moved more than this from the last posted one. Below it the change is inside the min-RTT estimator's own noise, and re-posting would churn measured_at without improving the offset.
